plan:
EXPERIMENT DESIGN — "Microbatch count vs. throughput for 1F1B, 1F1B-I, ZB-1p, ZB-2p"
DESIGN-ONLY DELIVERABLE. No experiment was run. All numbers below are ILLUSTRATIVE, produced by the simulation model specified here, NOT empirical measurements.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
0. OBJECTIVE & HYPOTHESIS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Question: Does throughput for 1F1B, 1F1B-I, and ZB-1p improve as the number of microbatches (m) increases, while ZB-2p maintains high throughput even at few microbatches?

Compound hypothesis to test:
  (H1) Throughput of 1F1B, 1F1B-I, and ZB-1p is monotonically non-decreasing in m over m∈{1,2,4,8,16,32}, driven by a shrinking pipeline bubble.
  (H2) ZB-2p reaches ≥90% of its m=32 throughput already at m=1 or m=2 (near-flat throughput curve).
  (H3, supporting) At low m (1–2), ZB-2p throughput materially exceeds 1F1B and ZB-1p at the same m (their bubbles are large when m is small).

Because /workspace contains no code (verified: only task.json exists) and the sandbox has no GPU, the experiment is a discrete-event SCHEDULATION SIMULATION of the four pipeline schedules. The design is specified so a competent engineer can implement the simulator in an afternoon.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1. METHOD SEMANTICS (locked in; each is an ASSUMPTION grounded in the standard pipeline-parallelism literature, since the repo has no code to confirm them)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• 1F1B (One Forward One Backward). Baseline non-interleaved schedule. Each stage ramps up to (P−1) in-flight microbatches, then alternates one forward / one backward. Residual fill+drain bubble ≈ (P−1)(t_f+t_b) of idle time per iteration, so bubble FRACTION ≈ (P−1)/(m+P−1) → 0 only as m→∞. This is the reference; throughput must be bought by increasing m.

• 1F1B-I (interleaved 1F1B). Each physical stage holds V=2 virtual stages (4 of the 32 layers each) and the schedule interleaves forward/backward across the virtual sub-stages. Standard result (DeepSpeed/HetPipe-style interleaving): total per-stage compute is unchanged, but the bubble is reduced by a factor V, so bubble fraction ≈ (P−1)/(V·(m+…)). Consequence: reaches its asymptote at lower m than plain 1F1B. Cost: finer-grained virtual stages increase activation memory and communication events per stage. (Alternative reading considered: "I" could mean "incremental/in-place" backprop rather than interleaving; I choose interleaving because it is the conventional 1F1B variant that interacts with microbatch count, matching the question's framing. Flagged as an assumption.)

• ZB-1p (Zero-Bubble, 1 pipeline). The zero-bubble family's single-pipeline variant. It is scheduled to OVERLAP inter-stage communication with compute (removing the comm bubble) but still runs one in-flight pipeline, so it retains a residual compute bubble ∝ (P−1)/m. Net: slightly better than 1F1B at small m (comm hidden), and it still improves with m.

• ZB-2p (Zero-Bubble, 2 pipelines). Runs TWO in-flight pipelines so that while pipeline A drains, pipeline B fills; the stage is never idle, so the fill/drain bubble is eliminated (bubble ≈ 0 for all m). Cost: ~2× activation memory per stage. Consequence: near-flat, high throughput across m — the method the question says should "maintain high throughput even with fewer microbatches." (Assumption: "p" = number of concurrently in-flight pipelines; alternative reading of 1p/2p as "1/2 phases" is less consistent with the memory/throughput tradeoff described, so I adopt the in-flight-pipelines reading.)

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
2. SIMULATION MODEL (implementable spec)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Fixed per-stage, per-microbatch time constants (milliseconds). t_f is calibrated so a 4-stage 7B model at these values lands near ~30% MFU on an A100-class device (self-consistent with the MFU check in §4):
  t_f = 76 ms   (forward, one microbatch, one stage)
  t_b = 152 ms  (backward, one microbatch, one stage; t_b ≈ 2·t_f)
  t_c = 1 ms    (point-to-point activation send/receive between adjacent stages)
Derivation of t_f: 7B model, forward FLOPs/token ≈ 2N = 1.4e10; per stage (1/4 of 32 layers) ≈ 3.5e9 FLOPs/token; per microbatch (b=1, seq=2048) ≈ 7.2e12 FLOPs; at ~95 TFLOP/s effective (≈30% of 312 TFLOP/s A100 BF16 peak) ≈ 76 ms. Absolute scale is reproducible and can be rescaled; the bubble-fraction and throughput-RATIO claims are scale-invariant.

Throughput definition (dependent variable):
  tokens_per_iteration M = m · b · seq = m · 1 · 2048 = 2048·m
  throughput(m) = M / T_iter(m)   [tokens/sec], where T_iter is the steady-state per-iteration makespan.
  MFU(m) = 6·N·M / (T_iter · P · F_peak), N=7e9, P=4, F_peak=3.12e14 FLOP/s. (6N = 2N fwd + 4N bwd per token.)
  bubble_frac(m) = idle_time / T_iter.

Per-method schedule logic (Gantt / pseudocode-level). P=4, m microbatches, each stage does m forwards + m backwards:

  1F1B:   T_iter = (m + P−1)·(t_f + t_b) + (m + P−1)·t_c
          (comm exposed, not overlapped; fill = P−1 slots, drain = P−1 slots)
          bubble = (P−1)·(t_f+t_b);  bubble_frac = (P−1)/(m+P−1)

  1F1B-I: T_iter = (m + (P−1)/V)·(t_f + t_b) + (m + (P−1)/V)·t_c,  V=2
          (interleaving divides bubble by V; total compute unchanged)
          bubble = (P−1)(t_f+t_b)/V;  bubble_frac = (P−1)/V / (m+(P−1)/V)

  ZB-1p:  T_iter = (m + P−1)·(t_f + t_b) + (P−1)·t_c
          (steady-state comm OVERLAPPED with compute; only the one-time fill
           comm is exposed; residual compute bubble remains)
          bubble ≈ (P−1)(t_f+t_b);  bubble_frac ≈ 3·(t_f+t_b)/T_iter

  ZB-2p:  T_iter = m·(t_f + t_b) + (P−1)·t_c
          (two in-flight pipelines overlap fill/drain → no compute bubble;
           only a fixed residual comm term remains)
          bubble ≈ (P−1)·t_c;  bubble_frac ≈ (P−1)·t_c / T_iter

Implementation: a discrete-event loop per stage (stage i, time advances by events) OR the closed-form T_iter above (both should agree; use closed-form for the headline table, DED for a sanity cross-check). Output a (method × m) table of T_iter, throughput, MFU, bubble_frac, and render one line chart (throughput vs m, 4 lines) plus two secondary charts (bubble_frac vs m; MFU vs m). Pure-Python stdlib is sufficient.

Illustrative results (FROM THE MODEL ABOVE, NOT EMPIRICAL), tokens/sec:
  m :  1F1B  1F1B-I  ZB-1p  ZB-2p
  1 : 2236   3577   2238   8866
  2 : 3577   5110   3583   8924
  4 : 5110   6504   5104   8953
  8 : 6504   7531   6525   8968
 16 : 7519   8298   7559   8975
 32 : 8177   8548   8210   8979
  bubble_frac: 1F1B  .75→.086 ; 1F1B-I .60→.045 ; ZB-1p .75→.085 ; ZB-2p .013→.0004
  MFU (illustrative peaks ~0.28–0.30): 1F1B m=32 ≈0.276 ; ZB-2p m=32 ≈0.302.
  ZB-2p m=1/m=32 ratio = 8866/8979 ≈ 0.987 (≥0.90). ZB-2p m=1 (8866) ≫ 1F1B m=1 (2236).
These values are placeholders the real simulator must reproduce; they are not measurements.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
3. FACTORS & CONTROLS (clean factorial design)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Independent (grouping) factor: method — 4 levels {1F1B, 1F1B-I, ZB-1p, ZB-2p}.
Independent factor: microbatch count m — 6 levels {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}.
Design: 4 × 6 = 24 cells, fully crossed.
Fixed (held constant across all cells):
  Model = Llama-7B, 32 transformer layers; P = 4 pipeline stages (8 layers/stage, evenly divisible);
  per-microbatch batch b = 1 (global batch = m); sequence length = 2048;
  hardware = single node, one GPU per stage (4 GPUs), no cross-node comm;
  t_f = 76 ms, t_b = 152 ms, t_c = 1 ms (fixed for reproducibility);
  measurement = STEADY-STATE per-iteration makespan (pipeline full; warmup excluded).
Randomization/ordering: not applicable to a deterministic simulator, but the code should iterate cells in a fixed order and, for the DED cross-check, seed any stochastic comm jitter identically per cell.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
4. ANALYSIS PLAN & PASS/FAIL CRITERIA
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Primary: throughput (tokens/sec) vs m, line chart, 4 lines.
Secondary: bubble_frac vs m (line chart); MFU vs m (line chart).

H1 (1F1B, 1F1B-I, ZB-1p improve with m) — PASS if, for each of the three methods:
  (a) throughput is monotonically non-decreasing across the 6 m-levels;
  (b) bubble_frac is strictly decreasing across the 6 m-levels; AND
  (c) throughput(m=32) ≥ 1.5 × throughput(m=1) (a meaningful, not marginal, gain).
FAIL if any method is flat/declining or the m=32/m=1 gain < 1.5×.

H2 (ZB-2p keeps high throughput at few microbatches) — PASS if
  throughput_ZB2p(m=1)/throughput_ZB2p(m=32) ≥ 0.90 (or, if m=1 is below bar, m=2 ≥ 0.90).
FAIL if the ratio < 0.90 at both m=1 and m=2.

H3 (supporting contrast) — PASS if, at m∈{1,2}, throughput_ZB2p(m) > throughput_1F1B(m) and > throughput_ZB1p(m) (i.e., the 2-pipeline method wins exactly where the single-pipeline methods are bubble-bound).

Expected outcome per the model: all three claims PASS (illustrative values in §2). The experiment is designed so that a real deviation (e.g., ZB-2p memory pressure capping throughput) would be visible as H2 failing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
5. FEASIBILITY & LIMITATIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
A discrete-event simulation is the right tool because the sandbox has no GPU, no installed ML stack, network disabled, and no source code — so no real training is possible, and the question is fundamentally about schedule-level bubble behavior, which a DED captures exactly. It captures: schedule-level fill/drain bubble, per-stage compute vs. idle, comm overlap (per method), and the resulting throughput/MFU. It does NOT capture: real hardware variance and contention, memory pressure / activation OOM (notably the 2× cost of ZB-2p and interleaving, which in practice can cap the achievable m or force smaller b), non-uniform layer sizes, attention vs. MLP compute asymmetry, and data-loading. The 224 CPU cores and system Python (stdlib only) are far more than sufficient to run the 24-cell simulation in well under a second.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
6. ASSUMPTIONS (mine) vs. FIXED REQUIREMENTS (from the brief)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Fixed by the brief / agreed: 24-cell factorial (method × m); model Llama-7B 32 layers; P=4; b=1; seq=2048; single node, one GPU/stage; steady-state measurement; t_f,t_b,t_c fixed to concrete values; primary metric throughput tokens/sec with MFU + bubble_frac secondary; H2 threshold ≥90% at m=1 or 2; do-not-claim-run constraint.
My assumptions (flag, confirm if needed): (1) the four method semantics in §1 — reconstructed from PP literature because the repo is empty; the "I"=interleaved and "p"=in-flight-pipelines readings are my choices. (2) t_f=76ms/t_b=152ms/t_c=1ms calibration (~30% A100 MFU) — arbitrary but self-consistent and rescalable. (3) V=2 for interleaving. (4) MFU uses 6N/token and A100 312 TFLOP/s peak. (5) Steady-state excludes the one-time fill; the residual (P−1)·t_c term in ZB-2p is treated as a fixed constant.
